newsitem.title: UK: UK fund managers more upbeat on UK shares-Merrill.
newsitem.headline: UK fund managers more upbeat on UK shares-Merrill.

text.p: UK fund managers have swung to a positive stance on domestic equities for the first time since 1995, according to a survey by investment bank Merrill Lynch.

The poll, taken by Gallup between April 7 and 9 and covering 72 institutions managing funds totalling $1,550 billion, found a "positive balance" of four percent planned to increase their holdings of UK shares.

The balance -- representing the difference between those planning to raise and reduce their holdings of a particular asset class -- compared with a negative seven percent last month and with a negative reading of near 40 percent at the trough of sentiment last June.
"Despite the upcoming general election, managers... plan to incrase their UK equity holdings for the first time since 1995," said Trevor Greetham, global strategist at Merrill.
"This in part reflects the fact that most respondents expect returns under a future Labour government to be broadly in line with those if the Conservatives were to win again."

Merrill said 35 percent of managers expect the returns through the next five years to be lower if Labour wins compared with seven percent who expected returns to be higher and 56 percent who expected no change.

Funds questioned in the survey planned to run down their substantial cash holdings and to increase their investments in domestic property, gilts and in Japanese equities, as well as in UK shares, Merrill said.
U.S. equities were also less out of favour, with a balance of just one percent planning to decrease their holdings compared with 13 percent in March.
The survey was of course taken before the latest Wall Street shakeout in which the Dow lost 148 points last Friday.
Among UK shares, the most favoured sector was pharmaceuticals -- with a positive balance of 8.7 percent -- while the least favoured was chemicals which attracted a negative balance of 6.6 percent.
Asked about prospects for world markets, a balance of 17 percent expected the UK market to drop on a three month view compared with 58 percent who expected U.S. shares to decline.
On a 12-month view a 39 percent majority expected UK shares to be higher while a balance of 19 percent expected a decline.
Some 56 percent of the funds controlled by the managers questioned are tied up in UK equities, with the balance distributed widely across the other asset classes.

Full results of the survey were as follows: Asset Class Balance +/- (previous survey) UK equities +4 (-7) US equities -1 (-13) Cont'l Euro equities +10 (+14) Japanese equities +21 (+18) Pacific basin eq. +7 (+10) Cash -21 (-6) UK bonds +14 (-7) Bonds outside UK +10 (+3) UK index-linked gilts +6 (+5) UK property +21 (+15)
